data.raw_text:
massive gratitude to the opportunity of being a freelancer

this sunny morning in LA, i headed out 40 minutes north to cowork with the KapturBox team and my car breaks down on the left shoulder of the freeway.

i have a 2015 nissan versa & IYKYK, but if you don't it's fragile af & I was spooked every second a car drove by & I felt the whole car shook.

but pops called triple A for me 🙏🏽, the LA metro found me sooner & took me off the road & the triple A did me a solid and turned a blind eye that it wasn't my membership.

talked to this 69+ yr old the entire hour in traffic all the way home & the mans hustles still with this gig and referring folks who get into accidents to lawyers and more. with this saved $100k in 2 years to build his retirement home in the Philippines.

i get home, find out my transmission is completely fried & I'm presented with two options (1) pay $5k+ to replace or (2) get a new aka used car.

weighing pros & cons, I'm choosing a new used car with the $$$$ in repairs on this Nissan. And its the 2nd biggest expense this month with my laptop crapping out on me too.

fast forward to ubering to my apartment tonight from my parents and i'm talking another hour with another 60+ yr old man clocking in for his second job of the day. works as a custodian and an uber driver, sleeping only 4-5 hours a day just dreaming about retiring to texas where his youngest daughter is at.

and i'm here left at the end of the day writing this whole shpeel to you only to recognize that living here is tough.

the normal is multiple streams of income to support the basic necessities like rent/insurance/food/gas/retirement.

and as a freelancer, there may be some instability as the millenials & boomers say. but there is no cap to how much you can make doing one thing for multiple people.

and candidly, i am struggling with this economy - forgoing sales to save for my present & future, for myself & my parents.

and i'm also so grateful for the opportunity to do so. and underneath the inconvenience of any obstacle are these wholesome moments of connecting with others.

i may have lost 5 hours of working hours today & have to grind tomorrow but its (1) bc i want to show up and (2) i'm so glad i got to talk to these guys and spend time with my parents before they went on their trip that I HAD NO IDEA THEY WERE GOING ON.

if you made it this far, i love you to the moon and back and invite you to reply with something you're grateful for today.

bc i'm feeling sooooo mushy.

p.s. shoutout to clients who were so understanding with the situation and patient on comms/deliverables. MUCH LOVE <3
